A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProReason and contain readable main text, tables, workflow diagrams, examples, and complete appendices. Renamed agents and relocated material can be matched reliably. Some internal reporting inconsistencies remain, but they do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, caption and reasoning assessments, token measurements, and failure examples, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds experiments with additional model configurations, distilled models, benchmarks, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: V3 adds a distillation procedure: generate reasoning traces with two LLM-assisted configurations, filter examples by answer agreement, and fine-tune Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct using LoRA to produce ProReason-VL and ProReason-Q3 (Sections 4.3 and A.4). The original five-agent inference workflow remains substantively unchanged; Reasoning Expert becoming Insight Expert is a rename.

E1.justification: V3 adds MathVerse Text Lite and the reasoning-related MMStar subsets (Section A.5.7, Table 13), expanding evaluation to reduced-text mathematical problems and questions emphasizing visual dependence. The four principal benchmarks remain, and A-OKVQA was already evaluated in v2's appendix.

E2.justification: V3 adds R1-Onevision-7B and the vanilla Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct model as comparators for the distilled models (Table 2). The efficiency comparison expands from ReAct alone in v2 Table 11 to Direct, VDGD, CCoT, CoT, and ReAct in v3 Table 3. The original accuracy-comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: V3 introduces two filtered training sets of 5,980 MMMU test examples, one- and two-epoch training budgets, and subsequent MMMU-validation and MME evaluation. It adds Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and Qwen3-32B configurations and elapsed-time measurement. Official-MME scoring reports are removed, while percentage accuracy remains. These include new experimental protocols, without establishing reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: Most component-replacement, capability-swap, agent-merging, retry, reasoning-assessment, and failure-case analyses are retained after relocation. V3 removes the correct-versus-incorrect CoT image-relevance analysis from v2 Section 2.1 and Table 9. It extends the existing efficiency analysis with runtime measurements and an MME-versus-MathVista iteration comparison (Tables 3 and 12).

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Retry allowances describe the inference procedure, and references to multiple tuning attempts do not provide statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial results for Qwen configurations, distillation, MathVerse, MMStar, runtime, and iterations. Table 2 reports MMMU-validation scores of 65.4 and 67.4 for the distilled models versus 53.6 for the base model. Original main-table scores for GPT-4o-mini and Llama3-LLaVA-NeXT-8B remain. Revised entries include A-OKVQA Direct 78.9 to 78.6 and preliminary Llama VDGD 42.3 to 42.7; official-MME and CoT image-relevance results are removed.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The workflow's symbolic description remains equivalent despite renamed response variables. The added training procedure does not introduce a new mathematical derivation or formal property.

C1.justification: V2 centers its contributions on proactive, decoupled inference and LLM assistance. V3's abstract and introduction add generating training data and transferring reasoning capabilities into ProReason-VL and ProReason-Q3 as headline contributions. The headline performance statement also changes from an improvement up to 15 points on MMMU to an average gain reaching 13.2 points.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive interpretations concerning transfer of LLM reasoning through distillation and the performance-efficiency balance of adaptive iterations (Sections 4.3–4.4). Section 6 expands discussion of accumulated errors and agent agreement to ReAct, ToT, and Insight-V. The original failure mechanisms remain, while v2's dedicated interpretation linking incorrect CoT responses to weak image relevance is removed.

D1.justification: V3 documents agreement filtering, training-set sizes, LoRA, learning rate 0.0001, zero LoRA dropout, and separate epoch budgets, and adds a model-role configuration table. V2's code-availability footnote and repository link disappear; the future-release promise remains. V3 Table 14 also lists Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as the Vision Expert where the prose identifies Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, leaving an implementation inconsistency.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands to recent visual-reasoning and multi-agent work, including VipAct, Insight-V, and R1-Onevision, alongside DeepSeek-R1 and newer Qwen models. V3 explicitly contrasts its approach with Insight-V's shared-LVLM design and discusses reproducibility barriers. Related work also acknowledges evidence that CoT can benefit visual tasks, revising v2's more uniformly negative positioning.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, preliminary observations, and related work. Detailed baseline descriptions and the main-text ablation discussions move into reorganized appendices, while the main text gains training and efficiency sections plus a consolidated analysis overview. Reasoning Expert is renamed Insight Expert throughout much of the document.

P2.justification: V3 merges the original main and LLM-assisted comparisons into an expanded Table 1 with an average column, adds distillation and configuration tables, and restructures the efficiency and supplementary displays. Several result tables are removed. Most example figures retain their design, but the two-agent and five-agent prompt figures exchange positions, leaving Figures 13 and 15 with captions that mismatch their contents.

improvement.justification: V3 provides useful evidence beyond v2's inference-time results: Table 2 tests transfer into trained models, and broader model, benchmark, and cost comparisons strengthen assessment of generalization and practical tradeoffs. These gains are partly offset by removal of the code-access link and official-MME results, conflicting model assignments in Table 14, and mismatched prompt captions. The net improvement is therefore limited.
